summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood private on-prem air-gapped deployment for regulated medical device analytics. Customer needs: fully offline updates, strict KMS/HSM and FIPS, inventory of GPUs and networking, audit logs and RBAC, procurement timeline Q3. Discussed dedicated vs private tradeoffs, network isolation, signed images, and proposed next steps (security pack, benchmark).
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Emily Chen (Apex Head of AI), Marcus Lowe (Apex Infra Lead), Sofia Ruiz (Apex Compliance)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, uh thanks for making time. quick round robin before we jump in, i'm jordan from redwood, ae on this account. priya is our se, she'll do the deeper stuff.
[00:15] Dr. Chen: hi, emily chen here. thanks. we run the analytics and model teams for device monitoring.
[00:22] Marcus: marcus lowe, infrastructure lead. i own on-prem and airgap processes.
[00:28] Sofia: sofia ruiz, compliance. i'll be evaluating security and audit requirements.
[00:35] Jordan: great. high level, we're here to learn about your constraints and see if redwood private on-prem air-gapped deployment fits. want to start with current stack?
[00:45] Dr. Chen: sure. currently models run in our cluster, it's kinda a homegrown inference orchestrator. we use a mix of p100s and a few h100s we recently procured. but, um, latency and scaling for batch scoring is a pain.
[01:05] Marcus: to clarify we have two datacenters, primary in midwest and DR in europe row, and an isolated lab for dev. the production site is air-gapped for patient data. nothing inside has direct internet. updates are delivered via signed USB media and a validated update pipeline.
[01:25] Priya: ok that's helpful. on the air-gapped note, do you have an existing process for accepting vendor images or do you require staged validation?
[01:35] Marcus: staged. we have an offline image validation process — images are signed, scanned in a validation environment, then pushed via removable media. also all crypto keys are in our HSM, FIPS 140-2.
[01:48] Sofia: and auditors will want full chain of custody and logs for any update, so we need attestable artifacts. SOC2 is baseline, but we are moving toward ISO 27001 controls for the product team.
[02:05] Jordan: understood. redwood private supports offline deployments and we have a signed-image flow. priya, do you want to jump into the how?
[02:13] Priya: yeah. at a high level we package the runtime as a set of signed, versioned artifacts that can be delivered offline. customers can host the control plane in their VPC or on-prem private control plane. for strict air-gap we support an installer bundle + signed images; the bundle includes a checksum manifest and signature that you validate against your HSM.
[02:36] Marcus: sounds promising. question: what about model updates? our MLOps pushes models to a staging repo; we need to pull model weights into production in an offline-friendly way.
[02:46] Priya: common pattern is to ship model wheels as tarball artifacts, signed and hashed. we provide a small ingestion tool that runs in your staging network to validate signatures and then the operator moves artifacts across the air-gap. we can also provide a guidance runbook for the operator flow.
[03:05] Dr. Chen: how does redwood handle KMS integration? our keys must remain customer-owned.
[03:12] Priya: we can integrate with customer KMS/HSMs via standard APIs when connected; in air-gapped mode we support local HSM validation and key import processes. encryption at rest and in transit is enforced, and we can provide options for encrypted model blobs where the keys never leave your HSM.
[03:32] Sofia: is that compatible with FIPS and our auditor's requirements?
[03:36] Priya: yes — we support FIPS-compliant crypto primitives and can provide the crypto module documentation; we'd need to map to your control matrix.
[03:45] Marcus: network-wise we have Mellanox switches, 25/100g fabric, and a firewall layer. what's the expected throughput and GPU networking needs?
[03:55] Priya: for high throughput we recommend NVLink for multi-GPU model serving and 100g between nodes for KV cache sharding. but we can run single-host low-latency inference on single H100s or A100s. it depends on model size and batch profiles.
[04:15] Dr. Chen: our main workloads are medium-size generative models for telemetry summarization — sequence lengths typically 512 tokens, mixed real-time and batch scoring. target p95 latency for real-time is under 300ms.
[04:30] Priya: with an H100 and optimized kernels you can hit that for smaller models; for larger seqs we recommend model split or quantization. we have recommendations in our optimize toolkit.
[04:45] Jordan: a couple of questions on compliance: sofia, what are your mandatory must-haves to consider vendor fit?
[04:52] Sofia: must-haves: customer-owned keys, full audit logs accessible to us for 7 years (or exportable), SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC fine-grained roles, signed offline updates, and ability to run without external telemetry leaving the site. SOC2 artifacts are helpful but we may still need an on-site security review.
[05:15] Jordan: got it. we can share SOC2 Type II and ISO summary docs. for on-site security review, priya can help scope the checklist.
[05:25] Priya: on the topic of telemetry, we support an opt-out mode where no telemetry leaves the system; in that case our support access is through customer-provided logs/artifacts. we also offer a runbook for secure remote assistance that uses customer jump hosts.
[05:45] Marcus: can you talk about hardware requirements in more detail? we may not be able to buy a lot of H100s immediately; procurement lead time is long.
[05:55] Priya: absolutely. we can run on A100s, H100s, even T4s with quantization for some workloads. we provide a hardware compatibility matrix and a performance baseline table. for constrained hardware we recommend smaller models or quantized variants; Redwood Optimize helps choose the sweet spot.
[06:20] Dr. Chen: how do we do canary rollouts in an air-gapped environment?
[06:24] Priya: you can do staged rollouts by controlling which nodes receive the updated image; we support canary percentages, model pinning, and automatic fallback policies. that all works offline because the control plane lives on-prem in this deployment mode.
[06:40] Marcus: license and pricing question — are there per-token charges in private deployments or is it flat?
[06:46] Jordan: for private on-prem we typically do a capacity-based or seat/instance license (reserved capacity) rather than per-token. we can structure pricing as a committed capacity plus overage terms.
[06:58] Sofia: auditors will want an exportable billing ledger for chargebacks — is that available?
[07:03] Jordan: yes we can emit usage reports and token-level breakdowns, though in air-gap mode reports are exported locally.
[07:12] Dr. Chen: do you support model version pinning and reproducible evals? we need to reproduce predictions months later for regulatory reasons.
[07:19] Priya: yes — model versioning, deterministic seeds, and eval snapshotting are supported. we can store manifests that tie code + model + runtime version.
[07:30] Marcus: what's the usual lift for an initial deployment? timeline estimate?
[07:34] Priya: for a full private on-prem air-gapped deployment, typical timeline is 6-12 weeks from procurement to production for a bulk install, shorter if hardware and networking are ready. the first pilot (small cluster) can be done in 3-4 weeks.
[07:50] Dr. Chen: our procurement window is Q3, but we'd like a pilot earlier to validate latency and accuracy.
[07:58] Jordan: good — pilot makes sense. priya, we'll propose pilot scope.
[08:02] Priya: pilot scope: small cluster (2-4 GPUs), sample prompt set, baseline perf and quality runs, signed artifact flow test. Plan to run onsite or virtual depending on Marcus' preference.
[08:18] Marcus: onsite is fine for the pilot, as long as no external access is required. one more question: how do you handle emergency patches in an air-gap?
[08:28] Priya: we support an emergency patch bundle delivered as signed media; for zero-day critical patches we coordinate via the customer security channel. we also provide hotfix instructions that your operator can run locally.
[08:40] Sofia: and will you provide attestation that no telemetry or keys are exfiltrated? we need that in contract.
[08:47] Jordan: yes, we can include contractual language around data ingress/egress and attestations for telemetry. priya will capture the specifics.
[08:56] Dr. Chen: any limitations around models we can serve? we want to use some community open models and some proprietary models.
[09:03] Priya: we support a broad model catalog and you can bring-your-own-model (BYOM). for proprietary models you can keep weights on-prem and manage versions. we do advise checking license compatibility for some open weights.
[09:18] Marcus: about monitoring: we need long-term retention of logs and audit trails for 7 years; can redwood export those to our long-term archives?
[09:27] Priya: yes — logs and audit trails can be exported to your object store or SIEM. retention policies are configurable.
[09:35] Jordan: let's get into some edge-case questions — does redwood require internet for model tokenization or any external services?
[09:42] Priya: no, tokenization and runtime are fully local. the only external dependencies are optional telemetry and optional external KMS if you choose that integration. for air-gapped setups everything runs locally.
[09:55] Dr. Chen: what about continuous batching and KV cache? can we persist KV cache across restarts?
[10:02] Priya: yes, KV cache persistence is supported; for multi-host KV caching we rely on secure network links inside your fabric. we can also provide guidance for cold-start performance tuning.
[10:15] Marcus: network segmentation, we will need the control plane to be segregated and the inference nodes in a separate VLAN, is that supported?
[10:22] Priya: absolutely — we support arbitrary network topologies and detailed network diagramming during install.
[10:28] Sofia: a compliance question: will you provide evidence for change management when updates are applied? we need a signed trail.
[10:35] Priya: yes, our update mechanism produces signed manifests and a changelog that can be ingested into your change mgmt system.
[10:43] Jordan: quick commercial note — for pilot we usually offer a time-boxed pilot with engineering support and a small reserved capacity. if pilot is successful we move to a reserved capacity contract.
[10:56] Dr. Chen: sounds good. can i ask about staffing implications? we don't have a large infra team. how much operator involvement is expected?
[11:03] Priya: operator involvement is moderate up front (install, validation), then routine ops are minimal. we can provide managed services or train one of your operators. for full air-gapped support we usually include a runbook and 2-3 days of operator training for the pilot.
[11:20] Marcus: i wanted to circle back on GPU compatibility — if we can't get H100s for a while, will an A100-based cluster give us realistic perf numbers?
[11:29] Priya: yes, we'll provide benchmarks per-GPU type. the difference is kernel-level optimizations; we can provide perf deltas and recommended batch sizes.
[11:40] Dr. Chen: how about inference reproducibility across upgrades? we need to guarantee model outputs are comparable post-upgrade.
[11:47] Priya: we support pinned runtime and deterministic ops where possible; we also version kernels and provide regression tests that can be run as part of your CI.
[11:59] Jordan: moving toward close — sofia, any blockers from compliance perspective today?
[12:05] Sofia: nothing blocking; we need to review the security pack and probably schedule a security questionnaire. also legal will want a data processing addendum.
[12:18] Jordan: noted. we'll include a standard DPA and a proposed contract clause for no-exfiltration.
[12:27] Dr. Chen: ok, next i'd like to see a proposed pilot scope and what success looks like.
[12:33] Priya: pilot success criteria: p95 latency < 300ms for selected real-time flows, end-to-end signed-update test, and reproducibility test across versions.
[12:45] Marcus: thanks. i'll work on the hardware inventory and provide a list of available GPUs and network diagrams.
[12:52] Jordan: perfect. last things — competitors, any concerns?
[12:58] Dr. Chen: we've talked to an in-house team about building something; also evaluating managed APIs from other vendors but they don't meet air-gap needs.
[13:08] Jordan: understood. we'll follow up with the security pack and pilot proposal.
[13:14] Priya: i'll draft the benchmark plan and bring the perf matrix.
[13:20] Sofia: we'll need the SOC2 doc and a compliant architecture diagram for our auditors.
[13:27] Jordan: ok all. thanks everyone. recap of next steps: we'll send security docs, priya will prepare benchmark & pilot plan, marcus will share inventory, and we'll schedule the pilot planning meeting.
[13:40] Dr. Chen: thanks, talk soon.

-- End of call transcript --
